Subject: RFP Q14 — Exclusive tenancy & cross-region routing constraints

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security and infra teams are reviewing your RFP response but have a couple of specific follow-ups around data tenancy and routing:

1) We require clear confirmation that customer data for EU-hosted workloads can be guaranteed to remain in EU physical regions (no egress to the US) for logging, model inputs, and model telemetry.
2) For APAC customers we need the option for an exclusive tenancy pool (single-tenant node groups) and a routing policy that prevents cross-region fallback unless explicitly enabled.
3) We also need to understand whether your hosted control plane ever proxies request payloads through non-customer-controlled endpoints (e.g., US control plane for metadata).

Would appreciate a short write-up addressing these points and any attachments (matrix, diagram) you can share. Our procurement timeline is tight — aiming to finalize by end of month.

Regards,
Emma Johnson
Director, Cloud & Security
MedSys Health

Subject: Re: RFP Q14 — Exclusive tenancy & cross-region routing constraints

Emma — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to provide concrete answers and a short capabilities matrix. High-level answers up front:

- EU data residency: for hosted EU deployments we support physical-region pinning so that model inputs, logs, and derived artifacts remain in EU regions. We offer both soft-pin (policy-level) and hard-pin (customer lock) variants; hard-pin prevents routing/fallback to non-EU compute and is available as a configuration for enterprise customers.
- APAC exclusive tenancy: Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (VPC/on-prem) both support single-tenant GPU pools. For Hosted EU/APAC we can configure dedicated host pools per customer under an enterprise contract.
- Control plane metadata: Our control plane (control.redwood.com) is multi-region; metadata replication is asynchronous. We provide an option for a customer-managed control-plane for Private deployments. For hosted customers, a regionalized control path is used for EU tenants by default; control-plane egress of plaintext payloads to non-EU endpoints does not occur for pinned workloads — only metadata replication and health pings (pseudonymized) may transit our global control fabric unless you opt into isolated-control.

I'll attach a short matrix and an expanded PDF with configuration knobs, recommended audit settings, and suggested contract language. If helpful, Laura and Marcus can join a 30-min call to walk security through tech details.

Best,
Dylan
Head of Enterprise Sales (EMEA)
Redwood Inference

Laura — notes inline and confirmation below. Key technical confirmations we can assert in the PDF: 

1) KV/cache & model-serving locality: For pinned EU workloads we persist KV caches and model runtime artifacts on EU physical hosts. Our runtime will not proactively migrate KV shards to non-EU hosts. During catastrophic region-wide failure we support a documented failover mode; that is an opt-in escalation that we will only execute with explicit customer authorization (contract clause: "Emergency cross-region failover"), and it will be logged and auditable.

2) Control-plane endpoints: For hosted EU customers the default control-plane endpoint is regionalized (control.eu.redwood.com). That endpoint handles orchestration signals and telemetry ingestion for EU tenants. Metadata replication to the global control plane is opt-out; customers can elect isolated-control where no metadata leaves the regional control-plane.

3) Single-tenant hosted pools: For APAC we can provision exclusive tenancy pools under Dedicated or Hosted Enterprise with contractual isolation guarantees, physical host affinity, and dedicated network egress. We recommend Dedicated for strict tenancy guarantees.

4) Suggested contract language: provided in the attached PDF; includes audit windows, KMS key scoping per region, and SLA clauses for failover approval process.

I'll attach the verified PDF for Dylan to send.

Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Emma / Rajiv — please find attached our finalized responses and a concise capability matrix. Summary highlights:

- EU hard-pin: available for Hosted Enterprise, Dedicated, and Private. Prevents model I/O, logs, and KV cache data from leaving EU physical regions.
- Control-plane isolation: default regional endpoints (control.eu.redwood.com / control.apac.redwood.com). Metadata replication to global control is "off" for isolated-control customers.
- APAC exclusive tenancy: available via Dedicated or Hosted Enterprise with contractual host-affinity and dedicated network egress.
- Failover behavior: cross-region failover is explicitly opt-in & auditable; we provide an emergency runbook and a 48-hour human-approval window in the contract by default.

Next steps: if the package looks good, Marcus and Laura can join your security call next week (we have availability Tue/Wed) to walk the infra team through the diagrams and answer any follow-ups. If approved, I'll loop legal to draft the tenancy exhibit and intake the deal to procurement.
